- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2089-2101 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When a fix-up wait expires and the fix-up is still open, the code sets `wait_ended_at="${now}"` and patches the wait comment to done (2116-2118). The next run reads that time back (1867-1869) and uses it at 2257-2258, so an unresolved fix-up is treated as if it had resolved when the wait expired.
  WHY: A trusted "nothing to implement" re-block posted after the expiry passes the age guard at 619. The item is then closed as completed with marker fixup=none and the comment "no fix-up is pending" while the judge's fix-up issue is still open. The source severity was MAJOR, mapped here to high, and no other reviewer flagged this.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2089-2101 (open fix-up + expired wait branch, wait_ended_at="${now}"), 2116-2118 (wait comment patched to done), read back at 1867-1869, consumed at 2257-2258; marker at 624 and comment text at 629 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The wait-end timestamp that gates the new no-wait close is set to the current run time when a fix-up wait expires with the fix-up still open, so an unresolved fix-up is treated as if it had resolved at expiry. The next run reads the done wait back and never re-reads the fix-up's state.
  WHY: The fix-up has not merged after UNBLOCK_JUDGE_FIXUP_WAIT_HOURS (default 72). If the planner then re-blocks with the trusted nothing-to-implement reason (the #9215 pattern), the block is newer than wait_ended_at and passes the age guard at 619. The item is closed as completed with fixup=none and "no fix-up is pending" while fix-up #N is still open, and that fix-up may later open a pull request against a closed issue.
- HARDENING (not a finding): scripts/unblock_judge.sh | location: 1867-1869, wait_ended_at="${wait_updated}" in the done-wait branch
  PROBLEM: wait_updated is used as the wait end without a format check, while block_at (623) and fixup_closed_at (2106) are validated. A non-standard timestamp would make the comparisons at 619 and 1878 compare mismatched formats instead of failing closed.
  WHY: Suggested fix: validate wait_updated with the strict UTC regex right after the read at 1866, and leave wait_ended_at empty when it does not match, so the guard at 2257 fails closed. Estimated lines changed: 3. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.
- HARDENING (not a finding): tests/test_unblock_judge.py | location: test_nothing_to_implement_no_wait_keeps_the_judge_otherwise, parametrize list
  PROBLEM: Neither fail-closed check added in the last run has a test: the block_at timestamp regex at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:623 and the wait-without-end-time guard at 2257.
  WHY: Suggested fix: add one case with an empty created_at on the block comment and one where the done wait has neither updated_at nor created_at, both asserting the issue is not closed. Estimated lines changed: 6. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
- Overall HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.
